body: Quick pass on the final head: merges cleanly with main, gate quick 312/312 green (all first_traverse suites and example_catalog included), clippy clean, test count unchanged at 4324, body complete. Pure code move; no heavy lane reached. Ready for review.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 7fe32c8d0c1f8f7687c2655a20734525fe4f475f -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Thank you for this split. The review read the diff line by line, built the PR merged with `upstream/main` (6cfc0a6d4), and ran the tests locally on macOS.

### What looks good

- The change is a pure code move. The removed lines in `first_traverse.rs` and the added lines in `first_traverse_table.rs` are the same. Only these lines are different:
  - `pub(super)` on the moved items;
  - the `use` lines of the new module;
  - the provenance comment;
  - the `#[cfg(test)]` wrapper of the moved test.
- `first_traverse.rs` goes from 432 to 320 lines. The new module has 131 lines. Both are under the 400-line limit.
- The new module has a one-line provenance comment.
- The moved unit test stays: `operation::first_traverse_table::tests::the_catalog_tilted_pocket_clears_the_table_from_the_tool_change_height` runs and passes.
- The visibility stays narrow (`pub(super)`). No item becomes public outside `operation`.
- The body has a `Changelog: none` line and ends with `Fixes #3288`. The commit subject is a conventional `refactor`.

### Results (local, trial merge with upstream/main)

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | 321 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (36.8 min) |
| `first_traverse`, `first_traverse_table`, `first_traverse_table_tilt`, `first_traverse_posed`, `first_traverse_rotary`, `first_traverse_mill_turn`, `first_traverse_rotary_mill_turn` | pass (all in the quick plan) |
| `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work` | pass |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main` | 3 steps, 0 failed |
| `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` | 210 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (27.4 min, release) |

### Mutations (the moved code is a first-traverse collision law)

The moved code judges the machine table on a 3+2 plane. The review changed it two times to make sure that the tests still guard it after the move. The review reverted each change, and the tree is clean.

1. `table_read`: the up-axis branch always returns `Clear` (`<= Z_TOL` changed to `<= f64::INFINITY`). Result: red. The lib test `the_catalog_tilted_pocket_clears_the_table_from_the_tool_change_height` fails. `first_traverse_table_tilt::a_head_tilt_plane_that_a_move_from_the_tool_change_height_takes_under_the_table_is_refused_by_name` fails.
2. `tilting_all`: `Some(turns)` changed to `Some(!turns)`. Result: red. Four tests in `first_traverse_table_tilt` fail.

### Extra suites run

- No file under `testdata/` or a fixture directory changes. No importer code changes. Thus no extra suite is necessary.

### Goldens moved

- None. No `*.nc`, `*.cl` or `examples/catalog/**` file changes.

### Requested before merge

- None.

### Notes (not blocking)

1. `crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs:83`: the re-export is `pub(super) use`. Only `first_traverse.rs` itself uses these items. A private `use` is sufficient. The body says that `generate.rs`, `stamp.rs`, `rotary_traverse.rs` and `first_traverse_posed.rs` keep their paths. This is correct, but these callers do not use the moved items. You can keep it as it is.
2. The issue suggested a split at `in_user_frame` and the verdict mapping ("for example"). The table reading is also a clear domain seam. The review accepts it.

This PR is from an account without write access. A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
